title: World Action Planner: Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
summary: World Action Planner pairs the reasoning of a vision-language model with a multi-task, pose- and image-conditioned world model. The VLM proposes an initial action plan, then refines it by optimisation and search over imagined world-model rollouts rather than committing to the first plan. The authors report gains on compositional and novel-scene tasks where imitation-learned policies typically fail to generalise.
whyItMatters: Imitation policies fail on new scenes because they cannot check their own plan before acting. Making the world model action-conditioned turns it into a simulator the planner can query at test time, so extra compute buys better plans instead of more training data — the same trade that made test-time search work for language models, applied to physical manipulation.
